subject: On-prem control/data zones and egress proxy review
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmemed.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T09:12:00Z
Subject: On-prem control/data zones and egress proxy review

Hi Jane,

Thanks again for taking time to review the on-prem VPC plan with us. Attaching a first-pass diagram and a short checklist; the goal for this thread is to align on: control-plane reachability, data-plane isolation, and the recommended egress/proxy pattern for telemetry and optional model updates.

High-level assumptions (please flag anything that is wrong):
- Acme will provision a private VPC in your GCP project (no public subnets).
- Control plane components (control API, rollout manager) will be reachable from Redwood via a mutual TLS endpoint in a peered control subnet.
- Data plane (inference nodes) will be in separate workload subnets with strict egress rules; model artifacts may be pulled from our S3-compatible endpoint if allowed.

Open questions for Acme:
1) Do you require an outbound-only egress proxy (we proxy all external calls) or do you prefer a transit VPC with specific allowed peers?
2) Are there air-gapped constraints (no internet) for any clusters?
3) Which key-management service will you use for customer keys (KMS/HSM)?

Next steps I propose:
- You review the attached diagram (vpc-segmentation-diagram.pdf) and mark required changes.
- Confirm egress model (proxy vs transit).
- If proxy, we will share a minimal envoy config and port list for allow-lists.

Attachments: [vpc-segmentation-diagram.pdf (diagram, 750KB)]

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
---
Redwood Inference | developer-first LLM inference

From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmemed.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: On-prem control/data zones and egress proxy review

Diego,

Thanks for the clear summary and diagram — very helpful. A few notes from our side after an initial pass:

- We prefer a proxy-based egress model. Our security team wants all external traffic to go through a centralized egress proxy (company-managed) so we can do TLS inspection and DLP.
- We do have one environment that is effectively air-gapped (no outbound to internet). For that cluster, we will need a pull model where packages and model artifacts are staged internally (we can provide a bastion or internal artifact mirror).
- KMS will be Google Cloud KMS for now; we may evaluate HSM later.

Questions:
- If we use the proxy model, can Redwood support pinned IPs or do you require mTLS to a hostname?
- For the air-gapped cluster, can the control plane be configured to work in a "pull-only" mode (control plane updates pushed only via signed bundles)?

I'll loop in our netops contact if you want to set a short working session.

Best,
Jane
Jane Doe
Head of Platform, Acme Medical

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T13:27:00Z
Subject: Re: On-prem control/data zones and egress proxy review

Jane, Diego — quick technical clarifications from infra: 

- Control plane reachability: we support mTLS to a hostname plus client certs. If Acme needs pinned IPs, we can provide a small range, but failover could be impacted. mTLS + CN verification is our recommended baseline.
- Ports: control API (443), rollout manager (8443), metrics/tracing to collector (9411/4317 depending on collector). We'll provide a concise port list for allow-lists.
- Pull-only / air-gapped: we support signed bundles. For the air-gapped cluster, our recommended flow is: stage artifacts into Acme's internal mirror -> job on cluster pulls signed bundle -> local verification with Redwood pubkey. This avoids opening outbound to public endpoints.

Attaching the envoy snippet we usually use for egress (egress-proxy-config.yaml). Small note: the config assumes the proxy performs TLS origination to Redwood endpoints. If the proxy performs TLS inspection, we will need a config that supports mutual TLS termination at the proxy and re-initiation to Redwood.

/monica
Monica Patel
Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: egress-proxy-config.yaml (config, 4KB)]

Subject: Re: On-prem control/data zones and egress proxy review — action items

Jane — thanks for the quick responses and Monica for the config. Summarizing agreed items and next actions: 

Agreed:
- Acme will adopt a company-managed egress proxy for outbound traffic. Redwood will support both mTLS and pinned IPs; we recommend mTLS for resilience but can provide a routable IP range for allow-listing.
- Air-gapped cluster will use the signed-bundle pull workflow (no outbound to public internet).
- KMS: Google Cloud KMS. We'll update our deploy docs with KMS key alias and required IAM roles.

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Acme / NetOps: confirm whether TLS inspection will be done at the proxy or if the proxy will allow passthrough for mTLS. (owner: netops@edgepartner.io) — ETA: 2027-05-03
- Redwood (Monica): provide final port list and envoy snippet updated for both passthrough and inspection modes — ETA: 2027-05-02 (attachment: egress-proxy-config.yaml)
- Redwood (Karthik): publish signed-bundle format doc and a small validation utility for the air-gapped flow — ETA: 2027-05-04 (JIRA: INF-4521)
- Diego: schedule a 30-minute working session next week to walk NetOps through the diagram and config — proposed slot 2027-05-05 17:00 UTC.

Attachments included: vpc-segmentation-diagram.pdf, egress-proxy-config.yaml

If that matches your expectations, I'll lock the calendar invite and attach the finalized docs.

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
